findings.text: Fallback IOSF mailbox reports unavailable and data operations fail with a permission style error after emitting a warning, covering availability query plus read and write and masked modify.
Fallback PUNIT fencing operations are inert: acquire and release and the acquired assertion have no observable effect.
Fallback PMIC bus access notification registration, both removal forms, and chain invocation all report success without acting.
Quark mailbox unit selectors are HBA zero, HB three, RMU four, MM five, SOC forty nine decimal, and PMIC bus phases are begin one and end two.
Legacy IRQ normalization maps cascade value two to nine and leaves every other value unchanged.

AMD posted interrupt data associates a guest APIC physical location plus tag plus guest vector plus target CPU plus logging and guest mode markers plus opaque remapping state. Intel posted data associates only a descriptor physical location plus guest vector.
Remapping capability set currently exposes only posting at zero, and remap mode ordering places xAPIC mode before x2APIC mode.
Interrupt remapping parent lookup returns the x86 vector domain object.

Posted MSI is treated as active only when the build option and runtime enable and hardware posting capability all hold. Fallback build reports no capability, no-device for prepare and enable and reenable and fault handling setup, inert disable and broken marking and remap panic check, and null posted MSI acknowledge handler.

Stack call helper preserves the incoming stack pointer at the new stack top, runs the supplied call fragment with zero to three register arguments, then restores the prior pointer, treating condition codes and volatile registers and memory as clobbered.

Conditional IRQ stack entry has two paths: user origin or already in use stays on current stack under paired RCU enter and exit around direct invocation; kernel origin with stack free marks in use before switching and clears it after, with interrupts off in both marking regions.
IRQ stack discipline pairs RCU enter with exit around every handler invocation and brackets stack-switched execution with set then clear of a per CPU in use marker.

System vector and IRQ wrappers statically check handler and argument types then delegate to the conditional stack helper with argument passing for regs alone or regs plus vector; alternate builds without separate stack only bracket direct invocation; softirq helper forces in use around a stack call to the inner softirq routine.
Marking and clearing the hard IRQ stack in use flag is only sound with interrupts disabled; reentry or concurrent use without that exclusion can corrupt stack selection.

Low vector layout uses NMI two, first external thirty two decimal, IA32 syscall one hundred twenty eight decimal, ISA mapping as sixteen aligned external base plus IRQ number, and spurious APIC two hundred fifty five.

High system vectors descend from two hundred fifty four for error, then reschedule, call function, call single, thermal, threshold, reboot, platform IPI, IRQ work, guest mediated PMI, deferred error, hypervisor callback, posted trio, managed shutdown, HyperV reenlightenment and timer, local timer, down to posted MSI notification two hundred thirty five decimal, with a total space of two hundred fifty six.

First system vector is either the posted MSI notification vector or the end of vector space by build, external count is first system minus first external, system count is total minus first system, legacy IRQ count is sixteen, CPU limit is sixty four times CPU count and IO APIC limit is thirty two times APIC count, total IRQ count selects larger limit or legacy only by build.
IRQ work interrupt availability reports APIC presence on capable builds and unconditionally false on the fallback build.
x86 IRQ allocation legacy marker has numeric value one.
IOAPIC domain classification progresses through invalid then legacy then strict then dynamic, and its configuration bundles that selector plus domain operations plus device tree node.
PCI MSI domain creation is inert on this build and both native creation and default domain hooks are null.
Native halt primitives first purge per CPU idle buffers then halt, with safe form enabling interrupts atomically alongside halt; architecture halt wrappers delegate directly to the native forms.

Local interrupt control exposes save flags, separate disable and enable, combined save plus disable returning prior state, disabled test by absence of the interrupt flag bit, and restore that enables only when the saved state had interrupts active.
Jailhouse paravirtual presence check always reports absent on this build.

Static branch support records batch capability and emits a jump table record linking a code address and target and key; initial code is either a jump patched later or a multi byte no operation, and both query forms return a boolean selected by later patching.
KASAN shadow uses scale shift three with base from build configuration, start computed by shifting the negative canonical address range, and end as start plus one shifted virtual range.
KASAN early and full initialization plus shadow population, and memory and trampoline randomization, are inert on this build.
Default keyboard LEDs reflect NumLock exactly when a fixed status bit is set in boot parameters, otherwise no LEDs.

Die notification ordering begins at OOPS as one, continues through INT3 with DEBUG, next PANIC with NMI, next DIE with KERNELDEBUG, next TRAP with GPF, next CALL with PAGE FAULT, and ends with NMIUNKNOWN; register display modes are short, user only, and full.

Kexec control slots are numbered zero through three for physical control, virtual control, page directory, and swap page, with four pages total; debug handler occupies six units; control page is four thousand ninety six with code budget half that; relocation flags use bit zero for preserved context and bit one for incoherent cache.

Thirty two bit kexec permits full source and destination range with control limited to task size and 386 arch, while sixty four bit limits all three ranges to below maximum memory with x86 sixty four arch; cross crash check accepts 64 bit x86 machine type.

Thirty two bit kexec arch state holds top directory plus optional PAE middle levels plus two table pages, while sixty four bit state holds a control top directory plus separately allocated intermediate and leaf pages for the transition mapping.

Crash register setup duplicates supplied state when present, otherwise captures general registers plus extended registers on sixty four bit plus segment selectors plus flags plus current instruction address.
Relocation entry receives an indirection page identifier and is declared for both word sizes, with architecture image state marked present.
